items.stem: Priya says that to find the remainder when p(x) is divided by (4x − 1) you calculate p(1). Explain the error.
items.markingKey: remainder theorem uses the root of the divisor (R1); 4x − 1 = 0 at x = 1/4 (A1); so the remainder is p(1/4) (R1).

items.stem: A student claims: "y = (x² + 1)/(x + 1) has horizontal asymptote y = 1." Identify the error in this claim and correct it.
items.answer: The numerator has higher degree, so there is an oblique asymptote y = x − 1, not a horizontal one.
items.markingKey: The numerator has higher degree, so there is an oblique asymptote y = x − 1, not a horizontal one. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Explain why you should not multiply both sides of (x + 1)/(x − 2) > 3 by (x − 2).
items.answer: The sign of x − 2 is unknown; if it is negative the inequality would reverse. Multiply by (x − 2)² > 0 instead, or rearrange to one side.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: The sign of x − 2 is unknown; if it is negative the inequality would reverse. Multiply by (x − 2)² > 0 instead, or rearrange to one side. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Briefly explain why the identity A(x + 2) + B(x − 1) ≡ 3x + 3 can be solved by substituting x = 1 and x = −2.
items.answer: An identity holds for every x, so choosing values that make one bracket zero isolates each unknown.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: An identity holds for every x, so choosing values that make one bracket zero isolates each unknown. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Solve, without a calculator, the system of equations x + 3y − 2z = 13; y − 3z = 12; x − 2y + z = −11.
items.markingKey: eliminate one variable from two pairs (M1 A1); solve the 2 × 2 system (M1 A1); back-substitute (A1).

items.stem: The polynomial p(x) = x³ + ax² + bx − 6 has a factor (x − 1) and leaves a remainder of −24 when divided by (x + 1). Find a and b.
items.markingKey: p(1) = 0 (M1 A1); p(−1) = −24 (M1 A1); solve simultaneously (M1); a = −6, b = 11 (A1).

items.stem: Use your GDC to find the coordinates of the turning points of y = (x² − 2x + 1)/(x − 4), and hence state the range of the function.
items.markingKey: GDC turning points (A1 A1); range (R1 A1).

items.stem: Use your GDC to solve x³ − x > 6.
items.markingKey: graph both sides (M1); intersections 2.00 (A1); correct intervals (A1 A1).

items.stem: A student claims: "Partial fractions can be applied directly to (x² + 3)/((x + 1)(x − 2))." Identify the error in this claim and correct it.
items.answer: It is improper (equal degrees): divide first to get 1 + (x + 5)/((x + 1)(x − 2)).
items.markingKey: It is improper (equal degrees): divide first to get 1 + (x + 5)/((x + 1)(x − 2)). 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Use your GDC to find the real roots of −x³ + 6x² + 5x − 13/2 = 0. Verify that their sum equals −a₂/a₃ if all roots are real.
items.markingKey: GDC zeros (M1) (A1 A1); sum 6.00 = 6.00 (R1).

items.stem:
Let f(x) = (x² − 5x + 9)/(x − 2).
(a) Show that f(x) can be written as x − 3 + 3/(x − 2).
(b) Write down the equations of the asymptotes.
(c) Find the y-intercept and any x-intercepts, in exact form.
(d) Sketch the graph, showing the asymptotes and intercepts.
items.answer: (a) shown (b) x = 2; y = x − 3 (c) (0, −9/2); no x-intercepts (d) two branches approaching both asymptotes
items.markingKey: (a) division (M1) A1 (b) A1 A1 (c) A1 A1 (d) A1 A1 [Total 8 marks]

(a) Express f(x) in partial fractions.

items.stem:
Consider the system of equations x + 2y + z = 6; 2x + y − 2z = 6; 3x + 3y + kz = m.
(a) Find the value of k for which the system does not have a unique solution.
(b) For this value of k, show that the system has infinitely many solutions when m = 12.
(c) Find the general solution in terms of a parameter λ, with z = λ.
(d) State the value of m for which the system has no solution when k = −1.
(e) Interpret the infinitely-many-solutions case geometrically.
items.answer: (a) k = −1 (b) third equation is the sum of the first two (c) x = 5λ/3 + 2, y = 2 − 4λ/3, z = λ (d) any m ≠ 12 (e) three planes meeting in a common line
items.markingKey: (a) determinant or elimination (M1) A1 (b) R1 A1 (c) M1 A1 A1 (d) A1 (e) R1 [Total 9 marks]

items.stem: Explain why substituting x = −3 into 5x + 18 ≡ A(x + 4) + B(x + 3) gives A directly, and find A.
items.markingKey: the identity holds for all x (R1); at x = −3 the B term vanishes (R1); 3 = A × 1, A = 3 (A1).

items.stem: Explain why a GDC may report an error for a system with infinitely many solutions.
items.answer: The equation-solver expects a unique solution; dependent equations give a singular coefficient matrix, so no single solution exists.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: The equation-solver expects a unique solution; dependent equations give a singular coefficient matrix, so no single solution exists. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Ingrid says that to find the remainder when p(x) is divided by (3x − 4) you calculate p(4). Explain the error.
items.markingKey: remainder theorem uses the root of the divisor (R1); 3x − 4 = 0 at x = 4/3 (A1); so the remainder is p(4/3) (R1).

items.stem: Explain why y = (x² − 25)/((x + 5)(x − 2)) has only one vertical asymptote.
items.markingKey: numerator = (x + 5)(x − 5) (A1); the factor (x + 5) cancels, giving a hole at x = −5 (R1); vertical asymptote x = 2 only (A1).

items.stem: Nia solves (x + 6)/(x − 2) > 1 by multiplying both sides by (x − 2) and concludes that every x works. Explain the error and give the correct solution.
items.markingKey: x − 2 may be negative, which reverses the inequality (R1); (x + 6)/(x − 2) − 1 = 8/(x − 2) > 0 (M1); x > 2 (A1).

items.stem: "(x + 7)/((x − 1)(x + 2)) = 1/(x − 1) + 7/(x + 2)." Explain the flaw in this statement.
items.markingKey: Solve x + 7 ≡ A(x + 2) + B(x − 1): A = 8/3, B = −5/3. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Find the equations of all asymptotes of the graph of y = (−2x² + 8x + 5)/(x − 5).

items.markingKey: x² > 9 means x < −3 or x > 3. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem:
The system x + 2y + z = 3; 2x + y − 3z = 6; 3x + 3y + kz = m is given, where k, m ∈ ℝ.
(a) Find the value of k for which the system does not have a unique solution.
(b) For this value of k, show that the system has infinitely many solutions when m = 9.
(c) Find the general solution in terms of a parameter λ, with z = λ.
(d) State the value of m for which the system has no solution when k = −2.
(e) Interpret the infinitely-many-solutions case geometrically.
items.answer: (a) k = −2 (b) third equation is the sum of the first two (c) x = 7λ/3 + 3, y = −5λ/3, z = λ (d) any m ≠ 9 (e) three planes meeting in a common line
